A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForeSea framework and ForeSeaQA benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original ForeSea evaluations, ablations, retrieval results, latency measurements, and open-domain benchmark results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds hybrid retrieval, encoder and backbone comparisons, caption-only baselines, and surveillance subgroup analyses.

M1.justification: V2 introduces ForeSea-Hybrid, combining person-centric retrieval with global-frame retrieval, whereas v1 evaluates these separately. This is a limited procedural extension; the default tracker, multimodal encoder, and VideoLMM pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix B.2's VISTA-to-GCL terminology does not establish a backbone replacement, since v1 already specifies GCL-trained VISTA.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,041-question ForeSeaQA benchmark with six subtasks and text-only/image-text queries, plus VideoMME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench. LongVideoBench already appears in v1 Appendix B.3. The new caption controls and size/scene analyses use retained benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds predicted-caption and oracle-UCA-caption baselines and evaluates VideoRAG with VideoLLaMA3 in Table 3. Appendix B.2 expands the CLIP-versus-VISTA/GCL retrieval comparison to include SigLIP, SigLIP2, and EVA-CLIP. These substantially broaden the actual comparison methods, while Table 1's original comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds shared-backbone comparisons, caption-only controls, and encoder substitutions. Table 3 specifies a 64-frame LLaVA-Video comparison and hybrid retrieval budgets of two person tracks plus 24 global frames, or one plus 12 for LLaVA-Video. Appendix C.3 introduces size and scene stratification. These extend evaluation design substantially; existing benchmark metrics and default settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's spatial-grounding, retrieval-budget, and person-versus-global ablations, v2 adds hybrid retrieval tests, encoder sensitivity, backbone swaps, and predicted-versus-oracle caption controls. Appendix C.3 adds query-image-size and scene-type analyses. These address component dependence, visual-grounding requirements, and surveillance robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for model performance. V2 continues reporting point estimates; its additional subgroup results do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing main, latency, and open-domain scores are retained, but substantial new results appear. V2 Table 3 reports ForeSea-Hybrid at 66.9% accuracy/18.4 IoU and oracle captions at 83.2%/31.1. Newly evaluated VideoRAG with VideoLLaMA3 reaches 68.1%/9.9, versus ForeSea's 66.0%/13.6, revealing an accuracy–localization tradeoff. Encoder and subgroup results are also added. These are additional configurations, not same-setting improvements to the original ForeSea results.

T1.justification: The benchmark definitions, embedding equations (1)–(2), and temporal-IoU definitions and conventions remain unchanged. The evaluation-metrics appendix moves from C.3 to C.4 without mathematical revision; no new proofs or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The benchmark novelty, three-stage framework, and generalization claims remain substantively unchanged. The abstract corrects the claimed advantage from 3.5% accuracy and 11.0 IoU to 3.1 and 10.1 points, matching unchanged Table 1 values for ForeSea versus VideoRAG. This is a limited quantitative correction.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning backbone-independent grounding gains, complementary person/global context, caption quality, and scale robustness. Appendix B.2 shifts from justifying VISTA over CLIP to identifying retrieval limitations relative to newer encoders. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix B.1 claims Hybrid has the highest average scores, although Table 6 gives it 64.6% multimodal accuracy versus ForeSea's 65.4%.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly documents two-stage verification, removal of 50% of initial generations, Qwen3-VL-32B-assisted checking, and manual corrections. V2 also specifies global/hybrid retrieval budgets, encoder checkpoints, and 320×240 video resolution. These improve documentation, but do not establish that the existing benchmark was regenerated or its preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Qwen3-VL, EVA-CLIP, SigLIP, and SigLIP2 supporting the verification description and encoder experiments. The main related-work organization and positioning of ForeSeaQA and ForeSea remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten and tightened, Appendix B.1–B.2 discussions are revised, and new experimental subsections are inserted. The overall narrative structure, core method exposition, conclusion, and dataset-generation prompt templates are retained, making this localized editing and expansion rather than a wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 3 and expands the ablation, subtask, and retrieval tables. The latency and open-domain tables are reduced and placed side by side. All six figures retain their graphics, with changes mainly involving placement, table formatting, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V1's main RAG comparisons used different generator backbones. V2 Table 3 adds shared-backbone controls that separate grounding benefits from generator strength, addressing an important weakness in the empirical argument. Caption controls and surveillance subgroup analyses further strengthen validation. These gains are substantial despite retained best-accuracy claims and new Hybrid-ranking language that conflict with Tables 3 and 6.
